# BLUEPRINT-BINDINGS.md — every literal in Blueprint v2, and what replaces it

**16 August 2026.** `Star Shard v3 Build Plan/Star Shard Blueprint v2.dc.html`
is the shard surface, built. Every word on it is Justin's chart, hardcoded.
This maps each literal to the slot or computation that replaces it.

**Not `BINDINGS.md`.** That file is generated by `npm run bindings` and
inventories the `renderVals()` names the markup reads. This is the *copy*
contract: markup literal → corpus slot. Design owns the markup, Code owns
`renderVals()`, and the corpus is mine.

**Read `CHART-BUILDER.md` §2 first** for the three layers. Everything below
sorts into them: **A · FIXED** (28 portraits, shipped), **B · COMPOSED**
(784 combinations, not yet generated), **C · GENERATED** (the signature).

---

## 0. The one invariant

> `6 june 1989, 4:42 pm · portland, oregon` is the only birth data on the
> page, and it is rendered **from local state, in the browser, always.**
> It is never a binding fed by anything that has touched the network, and
> the generative layer never receives it. `PRODUCT.md` §8.

## 2. The combination — layer B, and it needs six sub-slots

Six literals in document order. This is the shape the 784 pass must generate.

| # | literal opens | slot |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | "a storm is a thing that has to break…" | `COMBO.06·10.lead` |
| 2 | "your sun sits in the sixth mansion…" | `COMBO.06·10.sun` |
| 3 | "your moon sits in the tenth…" | `COMBO.06·10.moon` |
| 4 | *(pull-quote)* "so the storm has to be conducted from a chair…" | `COMBO.06·10.pull` |
| 5 | "this is why the two most common things said about you contradict…" | `COMBO.06·10.tension` |
| 6 | "what it makes you unusually good at…" | `COMBO.06·10.cost` |

**784 × 6 = 4,704 strings**, ~350 words per cell. Pre-generated, reviewed,
shipped static. The key is `s·m` zero-padded — `COMBO.06·10`, not `COMBO.6·10`.

**The order is load-bearing:** lead → sun → moon → *pull* → tension → cost.
The pull-quote sits at position 4 because it fuses the two mansions, and the
two paragraphs after it are the only ones that talk about consequences.
`WRITING.md`: name the tension, never prescribe the virtue. Slot 6 says what
it costs; nothing says what to do about it.

## 3. The mansion portrait — layer A, shipped

**One component, rendered twice here and once per mansion in the codex.**
Sun's mansion first, moon's second.

| literal | replaced by | source |
|---|---|---|
| `the sixth mansion` | ordinal from mansion number | computed |
| `參宿` | `stations[n].kanji` | `stations.js` ✓ |
| `alhena · the twins' foot` | `stations[n].starGloss` | **MISSING — §6 supplies all 28** |
| `The Storm` | `stations[n].epithet` | `stations.js` ✓ |
| `4°17′ – 17°09′ gemini` | `stations[n].position` | `stations.js` ✓ |
| `your sun stands here` | computed — which of the user's points occupy this mansion, joined | computed |
| "every tradition that looked at this stretch…" | **`MANSION.06.claim`** | `corpus-mansions.md` ✓ |
| the four-tradition grid | `stations[n].crossCultural[]` | `stations.js` ✓ |
| "a brand, a storm, and a voice…" *+* "the medieval election books gave…" | **`MANSION.06.synthesis`** *then* **`MANSION.06.election`** — one paragraph, two slots | ✓ |
| "to be born under it is to be built for irreversibility…" | **`MANSION.06.archetype`** | ✓ |

**Three notes Code will hit.**

1. **`election` has two render positions.** In mansion 6 it runs inline after
   `synthesis`. In mansion 10 Design promotes it to a **pull-quote** ("the old
   books gave this mansion trade, alliance, and building. agrippa says it
   *'strengthens buildings.'*"). Same slot, two treatments — the component
   needs an `electionAsPull` boolean, not two slots.
2. **The dissent colour is a data flag, not a decision.** China's row in
   mansion 10 renders `#F878A8` where the others are `#F2EAD6`. That is
   `stations[n].match === 'DIVERGENT'` and nothing else. It now fires on
   exactly **four mansions — 10, 15, 21, 24** (`mansions-patch-aug15.json`).
   Every other mansion renders the grid in one colour.
3. **`MANSION.nn.keyword`** has no home on this surface. It is the ring label
   and the codex index entry. Not a bug — don't let it get deleted as unused.

## 5. Correction — the degrees on the flagship example

Three different values are in circulation. The ephemeris settles it
(astronomy-engine, 1989-06-06 23:42 UTC, 45.5152 N / 122.6784 W):

| | blueprint v2 | my reading | **correct** |
|---|---|---|---|
| moon | 26°49′ cancer | 26°51′ cancer | **26°51′ cancer** |
| midheaven | 5°48′ leo | 5°48′ leo | **5°49′ leo** |
| separation | 8°59′ | 8°55′ | **8°58′** |

Sun is **16°13′ gemini**, mansion 6. Moon and midheaven both land in mansion
10, so `6 · 10`, the co-location and *1 in 221* all hold. **These three
numbers should never be typed — bind them.**

## 7. The Farlight — new, and not in `CHART-BUILDER.md` §4

Design introduced this and it is threaded through all five screens. It is the
mansion **fourteen along from the sun** — the far bank of the road — where the
full moon nearest the user's birthday rises. It earns its place: it is the one
element on the blueprint that is *about a date*, and it is the bridge to
tonight without putting a transit on the shard.

**Computation.** One line, no ephemeris call:

```js
farlightMansion = ((sunMansion - 1 + 14) % 28) + 1
```

It is exact by construction rather than by approximation: a full moon *is* the
sun's opposition, and the sun returns to its natal longitude on the birthday,
so the nearest full moon rises 180° away — half of 28 mansions is 14. Justin:
6 + 14 = 20. ✓

**Copy — two slots, not 28.** Both paragraphs are structural and interpolate
the sun's epithet:

| slot | text |
|---|---|
| `FARLIGHT.intro` | fourteen mansions from your sun — as far from **{sunEpithet}** as the road goes — sits your farlight. once a year, the full moon nearest your birthday rises there: your sun in its mansion, the full moon in this one, facing each other across the whole sky. |
| `FARLIGHT.body` | it is the one night a year the sky reads your **{sunEpithetLower}** from the opposite bank. the hollow mark on your ring holds its place; the night it rises, tonight will say so. |

**`STATION.n.answer` already exists, 28/28**, written for exactly this case —
*"when this station is someone's Farlight."* Render it as a third paragraph
and the Farlight section becomes mansion-specific for free, with no new
corpus. Recommended.

**Ring treatment, already built:** a hollow mark (`r: 2.2`, `stroke: #9A8A5E`,
no fill) against the filled sun and moon marks. It reads as a place held open
rather than a place occupied, which is the right visual argument.

**Add to `CHART-BUILDER.md` §4** as a sixth component.

## 9. The ring — hardcoded to Justin

`renderVals()` in the x-dc block:

```js
const SUN = 5, MOON_MC = 9, FARLIGHT = 19;   // 0-indexed
```

Replace with `sigil` values. The 112-segment geometry, the 28-station tick
spacing and the `polar`/`arcPath` helpers are all correct and general —
**only the three constants and the `LABELS` object are chart-specific.**

`LABELS` is the nameable-mark requirement from `UI-PRINCIPLES.md`, and it is
satisfied. Its three strings compose from data already available:
`` `☉ your sun · ${epithet} · mansion ${n} · ${sign}` ``.

## 10. Order

```
me     784 generation prompt + review protocol ──┐
       SIG constitution + per-kind fallbacks ────┤
                                                 ├─→ generate 784 ─→ review ─→ ship
code   starGloss ×28 into mansions-table.json ───┤
       match flags + crossCultural fix ──────────┤
       farlightMansion() + FARLIGHT slots ───────┤
       shardReading() composer ──────────────────┘
       bind the ring's three constants
```

**`corpus-mansions.md` (140 slots) and `findings.js` are both done.** The
blocker is now the 784 pass, and it is mine.

**One thing held:** `findings.js`'s `seam` kind stays a no-op until the
nakshatra alignment question at the foot of `corpus-mansions.md` is decided.
`dissent` is unblocked and can ship now.
